name: U-Roy
hook: Talked over other people's rhythm tracks until three of his singles held the top three spots on Jamaica's charts at once, and the sound engineers call toasting was born.
blurb: Ewart Beckford, known as U-Roy, was already known on Kingston sound systems for talking over records when the singer John Holt introduced him to the producer Duke Reid in 1970. His first singles for Reid's Treasure Isle label, 'Wake the Town', 'Rule the Nation' and 'Wear You to the Ball', all reused existing rocksteady rhythm tracks with U-Roy talking, chanting and ad-libbing over the top rather than singing a fixed lyric. For twelve weeks in early 1970 the three held the top three spots on both of Jamaica's radio charts at once, and other DJs quickly copied the style, called toasting. He did not invent toasting, but he moved it from the dancehall MC's live performance into the studio and onto records people bought. That happened just as Kingston's dub engineers were learning to strip records down to drum and bass. The two ideas, an MC talking over a rhythm and a producer remixing that same rhythm into new records, are usually told as separate stories in this map's sources, but they came out of the same sound systems within a few years of each other.

signatureTracks.title: Wake the Town
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: His first single for Duke Reid, and the record usually credited with taking toasting into the studio.
